program_note:
An Autumn Flowering, written in 1992-1993, was originally the first movement of a three-movement symphony with the same name.  It was always intended to be detachable, as an independent overture, however, performable by a large chamber orchestra, or small full-sized orchestra:  if there are more than five stands of each string section, care should be taken that the strings do not predominate over the winds and brass in mm.13-48 and mm.140-end.

The title of the first movement reflects the fact that the form somewhat parallels that of a Swedish Ivy flower that began blooming in my studio as I began the piece:  as one set of three to five small flowers reaches maturity and then drop off, another set has already begun.  Similarly in my music, as one phrase or group of phrases climaxes, another group has already begun.

An Autumn Flowering is approximately 9:00 in duration.

David S. Lefkowitz

September 19, 1995

Los Angeles, CA
